feedback:
Decision: approve. The candidate is the best raced design (entityR2B, iteration 3, score 140.28: kp 3.0, kd 0.30, ki 0.30, base_speed 1.5, sensor spread x = ±0.024 m, footprint 0.016 m) with one change, the outer sensor spread widened to x = ±0.032 m. The weights stay antisymmetric at (-1.6, -0.8, 0, 0.8, 1.6), and kp, kd, ki, base_speed, footprint and line_loss (last_direction) are unchanged, so the step is single-variable. The evidence supports it: iteration 0 to 1 showed that widening the spread from ±0.016 m to ±0.024 m, together with the footprint change, reduced line losses and raised the score from 57.10 to 124.80, and iteration 4 showed that ki 0.60 lowered the score to 103.99, so the ki 0.30 setting is kept. Line losses remain at 1.7 on the oval and 2.0 on the s-bend in iteration 3, and max_error is still 0.061 to 0.063 m, so the spread is the main unexplored lever for them. The candidate is valid: all positions are inside the ±0.08 m limit and the footprint is in the allowed set. I make no claim about how it will perform. This is early-to-mid exploration with six iterations remaining, and the change is a clean step from the best raced design, so it should race now.

Read the next race as follows. If line_loss_events fall on the s-bend and oval and max_error drops toward or below 0.06, keep ±0.032 m and check whether the oval finish count stays at 3 or rises. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.25 on the oval or s-bend, which would indicate reduced centre sensitivity, set kd to 0.40 and keep the wider spread, since iteration 3 oscillation was 0.228 (oval) and 0.231 (s-bend) at ±0.024 m. If line losses are unchanged or worse, return to ±0.024 m and move to a different lever, rather than widening further.
